name: Reflect Orbital mirror (full scale)
note: Parity model for the v1.1 'Reflect Mirror' type. Body frame: +Z = mirror normal (sun_reflect_ground_site), +X toward velocity. One 55 x 55 m square membrane mirror (the quoted full-scale size) on a small bus. The CPU evaluator aims it with satGroundSiteIdeal(), the mirror of the GPU's lock-window aim.

sources.subject: attitude
sources.value: the mirror normal bisects the Sun and the chosen ground site
sources.source: Wikipedia, 'Reflect Orbital' (Earendil-1: an 18 m square of 'four triangular membrane panels' of 'plastic film coated in aluminum', sun-synchronous 600-650 km, a ~5 km spot, reoriented 'within seconds to keep its beam on a target'; up to 50,000 reflectors by 2035). The site choice, lock windows and slew are the app's TargetedReflector machinery (CLAUDE.md).

sources.subject: mirror
sources.value: 55 x 55 m square membrane mirror (3025 m2)
sources.source: Reflect Orbital's quoted full-scale mirror, 55 x 55 m (as specified by the project owner, 2026-09-24); the square shape of Earendil-1's 18 m demonstrator (Wikipedia, 'Reflect Orbital' (Earendil-1: an 18 m square of 'four triangular membrane panels' of 'plastic film coated in aluminum', sun-synchronous 600-650 km, a ~5 km spot, reoriented 'within seconds to keep its beam on a target'; up to 50,000 reflectors by 2035)).

sources.subject: bus
sources.value: 1 x 1 x 0.6 m black box behind the mirror centre
sources.source: Earendil-1 is a small satellite; its bus size is unpublished.

sources.subject: mirror_film
sources.source: Aluminised film. A ~5 km spot from ~625 km is ~8 mrad, about the Sun's own 9.3 mrad disk (Wikipedia, 'Reflect Orbital' (Earendil-1: an 18 m square of 'four triangular membrane panels' of 'plastic film coated in aluminum', sun-synchronous 600-650 km, a ~5 km spot, reoriented 'within seconds to keep its beam on a target'; up to 50,000 reflectors by 2035)), so the film adds almost no blur - near-perfect specular is consistent.
